enso.cpc_discussion: ENSO Alert System Status: El Niño Advisory   Synopsis:   El Niño continues to strengthen, with a strong-to-very strong El Niño likely through January-March 2027 (remaining greater than an 83% chance). El Niño strengthened further last month, with sea surface temperature anomalies exceeding +4.0°C in portions of the eastern equatorial Pacific [Fig. 1] . Most Niño indices increased in the past month, reaching +2.1°C in Niño-3.4, +3.0°C in Niño-3, and +3.9°C in Niño-1+2 [Fig. 2] . The equatorial subsurface temperature index (average from 180°-100°W) was well above average [Fig. 3] , reflecting a deeper-than-average thermocline. Subsurface temperatures remained in excess of +10.0°C at depth in the eastern Pacific Ocean [Fig. 4] . Low-level westerly wind anomalies and upper-level easterly wind anomalies stretched from the western to the east-central equatorial Pacific. Enhanced convection and rainfall persisted from the central to the eastern Pacific, while anomalies remained suppressed over Indonesia [Fig. 5] . The traditional and equatorial Southern Oscillation indices were significantly negative. Collectively, the coupled ocean-atmosphere system reflected a strengthening El Niño. The CPC Official ENSO outlook , which synthesizes multiple models from North America and abroad, indicates El Niño will continue to strengthen through the end of the year [Figs. 6 -7 -8] . Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service El Paso TX/Santa Teresa NM
620 AM MDT Sat Oct 17 2026

...New AVIATION, FIRE WEATHER...

.KEY MESSAGES... 
Updated at 528 AM MDT Sat Oct 17 2026

 - Temperatures remain well below normal on Saturday, but will
   rebound nicely heading into next week. Lowland highs in the
   lower 60s Saturday afternoon, warming to the lower to mid 80s
   by Tuesday.

 - Breezy east flow continues on Saturday, especially across
   Southwest New Mexico with midday gusts up to 30 mph possible. 
 
 - Dry weather over the weekend, then a slight chance for showers
   and thunderstorms on Monday. Long term forecast favors renewed
   rain chances area wide, especially into the latter half of 
   next week. Localized heavy rain could result in additional 
   flooding for some areas.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
Issued at 1100 PM MDT Fri Oct 16 2026

Overall weather pattern at the moment depicts a stagnant, orphaned 
upper low over Southern California, and ridging heights aloft
across much of the southern Rockies and Texas. At the surface,
high pressure remains fixed over much of the southern Plains,
extending west into Southern New Mexico and Far West Texas. 

East flow and cool October temperatures will continue into 
Saturday behind last Thursday night's strong cold front. We may be
in for the coolest night of the season so far tonight, dipping to
the upper 30s/lower 40s across much of the forecast area Saturday
morning. Temperatures will remain quite cool Saturday afternoon, 
with lowland highs only reaching the lower 60s. This is 10-15 
degrees below normal for mid-October. Winds will be lighter as the
surface high drifts east away from our area, generally 10 to 15
mph with some lingering gusty conditions along the AZ/NM state
line.

The temperature rebound begins on Sunday as cold air advection 
from the east lessens. Lowland highs should reach the upper
60s/lower 70s, an 8 to 10-degree warmup from Saturday. Moisture
increases out of the south may lead to more cloud coverage Sunday
afternoon, and maybe even some light rain showers across Southwest
New Mexico in the evening and overnight hours. No significant
rains are expected here.

Orphaned low finally opens up into a wave on Monday, progressing
east across the southern Rockies. Precipitable water 0.8-1.0" and
a slightly stronger 50-knot jet aloft should lead to scattered
rain showers and a few weak thunderstorms. Rain chances seem quite
spotty with this event, and any rain that does fall looks to be in
the T-0.10" range. No flood risk here.

Late week weather pattern favors a strong warmup in temperatures,
returning the seasonal averages (maybe even a bit warmer than 
normal) Tuesday/Wednesday. Models seem confidence in strong, 
meridional jet flow diving down the Pacific seaboard midweek, 
suggesting the development of a deep Pacific low and thus a 
favorable pattern for rain chances. Best chances looks to play 
out around the Wednesday-Saturday timeframe, but it honestly looks
like we're facing multiple rounds of rain chances with a train of
Pacific low pressure systems affecting much of the Southwestern 
United States. While QPF in late October will be generally lower 
than September due to the end of monsoonal flow, less convective 
potential, and speed of these systems, there is still a risk of 
localized flash flooding. Any heavy rains that fall will occur 
over saturated soils from the past few weeks.

&&

.AVIATION...
(12Z TAFS)
Issued at 528 AM MDT Sat Oct 17 2026

We will have VFR conditions today. There are some mid clouds
sneaking up from Mexico and that could give us some off and on
mid and high ceilings today of SCT-BKN120-150. By this afternoon 
we will have unlimited ceilings and those clear skies will 
continue into Sunday. At the surface we will see less winds today 
than yesterday, but most TAF sites will see occasional low end 
wind gusts during the afternoon hours, before we see generally 
light winds tonight. Rain and thunderstorm chances will return to 
the forecast for much of the coming week.

&&

.FIRE WEATHER...
Issued at 528 AM MDT Sat Oct 17 2026

We will see less winds today after yesterday's strong winds. Our
winds will be out of the east today and will be occasionally
gusty, but the winds will stay below critical levels. The min RH's
today will be in the mid to upper teens in the lowlands and in the
20's in area mountains. On Sunday we will see the start of a
warming trend along with an increase in moisture. Min RH's values
on Sunday and through most of the coming week, will run at or
above 30%. Rain chances return to forecast, first west of the Rio
Grande on Sunday and then across most of the region each day this
coming week.
